A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Charm research work, with complete, readable main text, references and supplementary Sections 6–20. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT fine-tuning experiments on image aesthetic and quality assessment datasets, together with ablations and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and appendix analyses, with revised AVA baseline values in Table 1.

M1.justification: Tokenization, patch selection, position and scale embeddings, fine-tuning losses, and the three-scale variant are unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same coverage: AVA, AADB, TAD66k, PARA and BAID for aesthetic assessment, and SPAQ and KonIQ10k for quality assessment. No test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including Table 2, the AnyRes comparison in Appendix 6, and Tables 15–16. Table 1 retains the named standard Dinov2-small baseline while changing its scores.

E3.justification: The stated preprocessing, splits, backbones, token budgets, optimization settings and evaluation metrics are identical. No protocol or model-setting revision accompanies the Table 1 numerical update.

E4.justification: The tokenization, patch-selection, scale, augmentation, input-length, convergence and computational-cost analyses are unchanged, including all supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Five-split median reporting for SPAQ and KonIQ10k, five-run averaging in Figure 10, and the standard-deviation information in Table 16 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the AVA baseline PLCC/SRCC/ACC from 0.710/0.706/0.802 to 0.734/0.732/0.808. Charm remains at 0.779/0.777/0.826, so displayed gains decrease from 6.9%/7.1%/2.4% to 4.5%/4.5%/1.8%. This is a localized result revision; all other results, including appendix entries, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The patch-count and multiscale mathematical definitions in Section 3 and Appendix 7 are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same preservation, compatibility, efficiency and performance claims, including the abstract's improvement of up to 8.1%.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning random patch selection, overfitting, computational tradeoffs, information loss and Swin incompatibility are unchanged. No explanation of the revised AVA baseline is added.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing instructions and the code/pretrained-model access statement and link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The 54 cited works, related-work discussion and supplementary positioning against existing approaches are identical.

P1.justification: Only the administrative arXiv version/date stamp changes, from v1 dated 3 April 2025 to v2 dated 15 May 2025. Prose, headings, terminology and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions and placement are unchanged. Table 1 only substitutes numerical values; rendered-page comparison reveals no accompanying display or layout revision.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 1 baseline now agrees with Table 3, but Tables 6, 10 and 13 retain the earlier Dinov2-small values. Table 13 assigns the revised values to Dinov2-large. Neither PDF explains this discrepancy or identifies a changed setting. The update reduces reported gains, but whether it corrects an error or introduces a model/value mismatch remains unresolved, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
